title: Essere e Avere
subtitle: The two most essential verbs in Italian — irregular, and used everywhere.
objectives: Conjugate essere (to be) in the present tense
Conjugate avere (to have) in the present tense
Use avere in fixed expressions like avere fame and avere ... anni

content.intro: Essere and avere are the two pillars of Italian: you'll use them in almost every sentence, and later they're also the building blocks of the passato prossimo (compound past tense).
content.explanation: Both verbs are irregular and must be memorized — but they're used so constantly that this happens naturally with practice. Essere expresses identity, origin, characteristics and location (with certain expressions); avere expresses possession, but also age, and a large family of physical/emotional-state expressions where English uses “to be”.

rules.heading: a) Essere
rules.body:
• Identity/profession: Sono Marco. Sei insegnante.
  • Origin: Siamo di Milano.
  • Characteristics: È simpatica.

rules.heading: b) Avere — possession and age
rules.body:
• Possession: Ho una macchina.
  • Age (never essere here): Ho trent'anni. (I am thirty — literally "I have thirty years")

rules.heading: c) Avere in fixed expressions
rules.body:
• avere fame/sete — to be hungry/thirsty
  • avere caldo/freddo — to be hot/cold
  • avere sonno — to be sleepy
  • avere paura (di) — to be afraid (of)
  • avere ragione/torto — to be right/wrong
  • avere fretta — to be in a hurry
  • avere bisogno di — to need

examples.it: Io sono italiano, ma abito in Spagna.
examples.en: I am Italian, but I live in Spain.
Do you have brothers or sisters?
We're hungry, shall we eat something?

commonMistakes.why: Age uses avere in Italian, not essere — a direct English-to-Italian translation of "I am" is wrong here.
Physical/emotional states like hunger use avere, not essere, even though English says "I am hungry."
Ha is the lui/lei form; io always pairs with ho.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of essere or avere.

items.explanation: Io + essere (identity/profession) = sono.
Loro + avere (possession) = hanno.
Avere fame — to be hungry — needs avere: abbiamo.
Origin uses essere: tu + essere = sei.

items.prompt: How do you say "I am thirty years old"?
items.explanation: Age always uses avere in Italian.
Avere sonno is a fixed expression meaning "to be sleepy".
Age needs avere, not essere.
Io always takes ho, never ha (which is the lui/lei form).
Voi + essere = siete.
Lui + avere (possession) = ha.
Avere freddo — to be cold — needs avere: ho.
Loro + essere (characteristic) = sono.
Avere ragione — to be right — needs avere: hai.
Noi + essere (characteristic) = siamo.
Avere paura — to be afraid — needs avere: ha.
Origin uses essere: io + essere = sono.
Avere fretta is the fixed expression for "to be in a hurry".
Avere torto means "to be wrong", the opposite of avere ragione.

items.prompt: How do you say "we need a hotel"?
items.explanation: Avere bisogno di is the fixed expression for "to need".

items.prompt: Which is correct for "they are cold"?
items.explanation: Avere freddo is the fixed expression Italian uses for feeling cold.
Siete is the voi form of essere.

items.prompt: Which verb form matches "noi" for avere?
items.explanation: Noi + avere = abbiamo.

items.prompt: "Sei simpatico" uses essere because it expresses...
items.explanation: Describing a personal quality uses essere, not avere.

items.statement: Avere is used to express someone's age in Italian.
items.explanation: Age always uses avere, e.g. ho vent'anni.

items.statement: Essere is used for physical states like hunger and thirst.
items.explanation: Avere is used for these fixed expressions: avere fame, avere sete.

items.statement: The io form of avere is ho.
items.explanation: Io ho is the first-person singular of avere.

items.statement: The tu form of essere is sei.
items.explanation: Tu sei is the second-person singular of essere.
Avere ragione means "to be right"; avere sete means "to be thirsty".

items.statement: Noi abbiamo and noi siamo are both irregular present-tense forms.
items.explanation: Both essere and avere are fully irregular in the present tense.

items.statement: Loro sono and loro hanno share the same verb ending.
items.explanation: Sono and hanno are each their own irregular form — they don't share an ending pattern.

summary: Essere = identity, origin, characteristics; avere = possession and age.
Age, hunger, thirst, heat/cold, fear, being right/wrong all use avere in Italian, unlike English "to be".
Both verbs are irregular — memorize the six forms: sono/sei/è/siamo/siete/sono and ho/hai/ha/abbiamo/avete/hanno.
